gen-gf-phudu-gf-gayathri: Gayathri keeps its curves open-ended and its thick-thin shifts mild, like a letterpress slug. Gayathri sits under Phudu's stencil-steady, bold display letters and lets them do the shouting.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-google-sans: Phudu is bold and unmistakable, drawn with a ballpoint's pressure-free line. Google Sans follows in a plain sans, with no thick-thin shift and terminals pulled well back, so the heading's openness carries down into the text.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-google-sans-flex: Modern and professional, Google Sans Flex ends every stroke as if cut from one ribbon, each curve finishing in a clean gap. Phudu's bold, distinctive display letters above it are the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gothic-a1: Gothic A1 is approachable, with a splayed c terminal that gives its sans text a friendly lilt. And Phudu does the loud work best, its rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord, while Gothic A1 simply holds the lines steady.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gotu: Clean and modern, the sans Gotu has hairlines of reasonable sturdiness and e crossbars with open mouths. Gotu softens Phudu's never-varying stroke with a gentle thick-thin difference, so a longer passage would read smoothly beneath the heavy heading.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gowun-dodum: Bold, rounded and a bit cheeky, Phudu is cut with generous openings on every curve, and Gowun Dodum has a wide-mouthed a. Its plain sans lines look smooth as tubing beneath.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gruppo: Phudu looks like glass tubing bent into letters, with generous openings on every curve. Gruppo is the quiet one, a professional, clean sans whose curve endings never get near each other, while Phudu takes the attention.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gudea: Phudu's ballpoint-plain line and generous terminal openings make it instantly bold and distinctive. And Gudea, a plain sans with curves as thick as a drawn thread, is happiest at a modest size beneath it.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-hanken-grotesk: Phudu brings bold, distinctive display letters, each curve left generously open at its end. Hanken Grotesk, a clean, modern sans-serif with a wire-bent look and wide channels into each counter, does the quieter job of carrying the text.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-host-grotesk: Host Grotesk reads contemporary and neutral, its curves sweeping open rather than curling closed. Host Grotesk would carry a longer passage smoothly under Phudu's stencil-steady heading, keeping the text light while the headline stays heavy.
